messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: decode-pool-7 reported OOM spike on streaming workers (GPU:0..3). 48% error rate on /v1/streaming.generate. Paging on-call (priority P1)
oncall-bot: Escalation: paging matt (oncall) and deepa (infra)
matt: on it, looking at dashboards now. seeing spike in decode memory usage around 13:07 UTC, per-node memory jumps to >98%
deepa: grabbing logs from the runtime. initial hypothesis: runaway generation from a few client requests with huge max_tokens?
sara: support-lead flagged customer ticket #C-20312 reporting dropped responses and streaming disconnects starting ~13:05
matt: can we isolate a pattern? model variant gptx-decode-v2 or a header mismatch?
deepa: grep on request headers shows a subset of requests with `x-max-tokens: 1000000` coming from the same IP range. service proxy normally caps to 2048, but recent routing change in canary removed the cap.
sara: ack, that matches customer complaints — their app retried repeatedly, causing sustained tail growth
ryan: checked autoscaler logs: decode-pool-7 hit container restart churn (OOM) on 3 of 4 pods, kube evicted then restarted. backlog grew and proxy started dropping new reqs (503s)
matt: immediate mitigation: enable server-side hard cap and graceful reject for streaming flows. deepa can you patch the fronting filter now?
deepa: doing it. patching nginx-filter to enforce `max_tokens_server=8192` and apply to streaming route; will toggle on canary first then global. applying to pool-7 first.
deploy-bot: deploy start: nginx-filter/patch@canary -> rollout to pool-7 (pods rolling restart)
matt: also disable streaming fanout for the variant to force non-streaming path (temporary) so decode workers don't hold KV cache for long-lived streams. sara, notify affected customers that we're throttling streams temporarily.
sara: on it. Drafting message: "We’re applying temporary stream throttles while we mitigate an underlying runtime memory issue; some streaming responses may be truncated — we’ll follow up with root cause." need ETA?
matt: initial mitigation should reduce OOMs within 3-5 mins after restart. deepa, confirm once restarts finish
deepa: restarts finishing. logs show incoming requests still contain some stale header values from gateway A -> route mismatch. I've added a middleware to rewrite header to server cap when >8192. Patching now.
ryan: runtime metrics: memory pressure dropping from 98% to 65% on restarted pods. request drop rate falling. good signal.
oncebot: SYSTEM: Incident created: INC-2026-0814-oom-decode-stream. Pagers: matt (ack), deepa (ack), oncall-bot forwarded to SRE channel.
sara: customer message queued, will send once we have confirmation of full recovery
matt: action items: 1) keep throttles until gateway fix is validated, 2) rollback the canary routing change that removed server cap, 3) run a scan for any other services with missing server caps, 4) longer term: enforce max_tokens at proxy + runtime and add rate-limiter by token-rate per client.
deepa: can do 2 and 3 now. rolling back canary flag `proxy_drop_large_max_tokens=false` to true. kicking rollback.
deploy-bot: flag rollback initiated: proxy-config/canary -> revert -> target pools: A, B, decode-pool-7
ryan: quick customer impact note for incident timeline: affected windows 13:05-13:15 UTC; ~12k requests dropped, ~5 customers reported partial failures. Major impact isolated to customers behind gateway A.
sara: sent update to customers at 13:20 UTC. one customer replied with logs showing multiple streaming reconnects. escalated to SE for postmortem follow-up.
matt: verdict: immediate mitigations successful, OOMs stopped after server cap + rollback. next: RCA and follow-ups. deepa take lead on runtime fix and send PR for a safety clamp in the decode runtime that enforces a per-request token ceil and evicts runaway KV caches after 5s of inactivity.
deepa: will open PR and include unit + integration tests. Also adding a new metric: per-request token-requested histogram, alert when >95th percentile exceeds threshold.
ryan: operational ask: can we add a short-term spike protection: if a single client issues >X tokens/sec then circuit-break that client for 60s. Helps stop retries turning into storms.
matt: yes, add to backlog and prioritize. ops: update runbook for streaming OOM to include steps we did: patch filter, rollback canary, restart affected pods, notify customers, add runtime clamp.
sara: support-lead: capturing customer compensation notes in ticket. one enterprise customer flagged potential SLA impact, creating internal notification for sales ops.
deploy-bot: deploy complete: nginx-filter/patch@canary -> success on pool-7. rollback completed for proxy-config.
deepa: follow-up: PR #4723 opened to add runtime clamp + tests, link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4723
matt: thanks all. will schedule a post-incident bridge at 16:00 UTC today for RCA and to triage longer-term mitigations. closing active handoff once postmortem assigned. :thumbsup:
support-lead: noting participant handoffs: matt -> deepa for remediation, sara -> support SE for customer comms.
ryan: final telemetry check looks stable for 30m. marking incident as mitigated for now.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Please file postmortem within 72 hours.
